and per-row formatting in pure pipes, and judge a template expression by the work it does, not by its parentheses.
A pull request adds a cart badge that shows
, and the review comes back: "No function calls in templates, they run on every change detection." The same reviewer approved
accessor that loops over every cart line and applies discounts to each one. The rule flagged the cheap call and waved through the expensive one, because it looks for parentheses instead of work.
The belief: any function call in a template is a performance smell, and since a signal is a function,

The advice is old and was earned. Angular evaluates template expressions on every change detection cycle, and for years, with zone.js, a cycle followed almost any event in the app: a click, a timer, an HTTP response. A method in a template ran on each of those, and teams that hid a sort or a filter in one found it at the top of the profiler. "No function calls in templates" became the short version, and the short version is easy to enforce: look for parentheses. What it misses is that the cost was never the call itself. It was the work inside the call.
When Angular checks a component, it evaluates every expression in its template (interpolations, property bindings,
conditions) and compares each result with the previous one to decide which DOM nodes to update. Nothing is skipped because it looks like a property: a
runs it on every check, exactly like

. Since Angular 22, components use OnPush by default, so a component is checked only when there's a reason: a signal its template reads changes, it receives new inputs, or an event fires inside it. But every check still runs every expression.
Reading a signal is a lookup
doesn't compute anything. It returns the value the
already holds and, because it runs while Angular renders the template, it records that this component depends on
. That record is the reason you call it: when
changes, Angular marks the component for check without any
from you. The cost doesn't grow with your data, so reading the same signal in five places of a template is fine. Forget the parentheses and the NG8109 diagnostic warns that
doesn't read the value at all.

Pipes were Angular's template cache long before signals. A pipe is
